entities.summary: Margaret Stewart, Dauphine of France, was a princess of Scotland and the firstborn child of King James I of Scotland and Joan Beaufort, making her a member of the powerful Beaufort family. Born around 1405, Margaret was betrothed to Louis d'Orléans, the eldest son of King Charles VI of France, in an attempt to strengthen the alliance between Scotland and France. This union aimed to secure the Scottish throne for her son, James, and ensure French support for the Scottish monarchy. The marriage took place in 1424, and Margaret became Dauphine of France upon her husband's accession to the throne in 1428. She played a crucial role in promoting cultural and economic ties between Scotland and France, but her time as Dauphine was cut short when she died in 1445. Despite her tragic end, Margaret's legacy as a cultural ambassador and her role in shaping the complex relationships between Scotland and France continue to fascinate historians today.
